description: The bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks across various language families, with the horizontal axis listing nine language family categories—IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic—arranged left to right, and the vertical axis labeled “effect” ranging from 0 to 30 in increments of 5 (not 40 as stated in the caption). Each category contains six grouped bars representing six model configurations: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (pink), and XLM-B₂ (red), as indicated in the legend. The IE-Indic group exhibits the highest effect values overall, with the mBERT-R₂ and XLM-R₂ bars reaching approximately 20–25, and the XLM-B₂ bar peaking near 21, though not 30 as claimed. The Semitic group shows the largest error bars, indicating high variability, with some bars extending from near 0 to over 25, but not down to -10, as error bars typically represent positive standard deviations above and below the mean. The Uralic group indeed shows the lowest effect values, with all bars clustered near or below 5. The IE-Germanic group shows a general upward trend from left to right across model configurations, while the IE-Baltic group shows relatively low and somewhat declining values. Error bars are present for all bars, reflecting measurement uncertainty or standard deviation, and are particularly large for Semitic and IE-Indic, suggesting greater variability in those groups. The chart does not show any bars below zero, contradicting the claim of error bars spanning to -10. Overall, the chart visually compares how different multilingual BERT models respond to context masking across language families, with IE-Indic and Semitic showing the most pronounced and variable effects, respectively.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family. The horizontal axis displays categories labeled as language families, including IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, arranged sequentially from left to right. The vertical axis is labeled 'effect' and ranges from 0 to 40, with intervals of 5 units. Each category contains six bars representing different models or configurations: mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂, colored light blue, dark blue, light green, dark green, pink, and red, respectively. Notably, the Semitic group shows the highest variability, with error bars spanning from approximately -10 to 25, while the IE-Indic group consistently exhibits the largest effect values, peaking at around 30. In contrast, the Uralic group demonstrates the lowest effect values, with all bars below 5. The IE-Germanic group shows a steady increase across configurations, while the IE-Baltic group displays a slight decline in effect values across models. Error bars indicate the standard deviation, highlighting variability within each language family and model configuration.
